overview_heading: InKaPP – Stay Informed. Cancer Registry Data for Active Patients
overview_intro: If you have or have had cancer, your doctor submits certain information about your condition to the cancer registry. This data is anonymously evaluated and helps to continuously improve oncological care in Rhineland-Palatinate.
overview_highlight: Until now, direct access to this data was only possible through your treating facility.
overview_intro_closing: We want to change that – together with you.
overview_what_body: InKaPP is a project of the Cancer Registry of Rhineland-Palatinate at the Institute for Digital Health Data. The goal is to develop a user-friendly patient portal that gives patients direct access to their own data – secure, understandable, and practical.
overview_perspective_body: We don't want to design the portal without the people it's meant for – we want to build it together with you. Share your experiences, your expectations, and help us create something of real value.
overview_perspective_highlight: No prior knowledge required – just your perspective.
overview_learn_more_body: How does the patient portal work? Who can use it? And what happens during the pilot study? On the project page you'll find all the background information, goals, and current developments around InKaPP – from the technical implementation to patient participation.

tutorial_step_legend_description: The date axis shows the months in which oncological events were documented. Each dot marks the beginning of a month.
tutorial_step_spot_description: Circles represent events that occurred on a single date, such as a diagnosis or a single examination.
tutorial_step_bar_description: Bars represent events that span multiple days, such as a radiation series or a systemic therapy course.
tutorial_step_diagnosis_description: Diagnosis entries document the cancer diagnosis, including the tumor location and the date of diagnosis.
tutorial_step_surgery_description: Surgical procedures as part of cancer treatment, including the date and type of procedure.
tutorial_step_radiation_description: Radiation treatments with start and end dates of the therapy series.
tutorial_step_systemic_therapy_descripti: Medication-based treatments such as chemotherapy or immunotherapy with the respective treatment period.
tutorial_step_progression_description: Progression assessments document whether the tumor is responding to treatment, remains stable, or is progressing.
tutorial_step_tnm_description: The TNM classification describes the spread of the tumor: T (tumor size), N (lymph node involvement), and M (metastases).
tutorial_notice_demo_data_description: This tutorial uses a sample dataset for demonstration purposes. The data shown is fictitious and is not related to your personal health data.
tutorial_error_load_failed: The tutorial could not be started. The required elements were not found.
tutorial_step_diagnosis_header_descripti: The header shows the name of the diagnosis and the date it was documented.
tutorial_step_diagnosis_icd10_descriptio: The ICD-10 code is the international classification of the disease. It describes the type and location of the tumor using a standardized system.
tutorial_step_diagnosis_laterality_descr: The laterality indicates on which side of the body the tumor was found — left, right, bilateral, or not applicable.
tutorial_step_diagnosis_morphology_descr: Morphology describes the tissue type and behavior of the tumor. It provides information about the cell type and degree of differentiation.
tutorial_step_diagnosis_topography_descr: Topography indicates the exact site of origin of the tumor in the body, based on the ICD-O-3 classification.
tutorial_step_diagnosis_histology_descri: Histological findings are based on the microscopic examination of tissue samples. They provide detailed information about the tumor type.
tutorial_step_diagnosis_metastases_descr: Distant metastases are deposits of the tumor in distant organs. The overview shows which organs are affected and when the metastases were detected.
